headline.caveat: 0% confident-wrong is achieved here almost entirely BY ABSTENTION FROM COVERAGE GAP, not by resolving conflicting evidence: SeaWeb's crawled corpus (sfblogs_20260727) is deliberately scoped to Travel & Hospitality / San Francisco Bay Area (see memory: travel-intelligence-target-lock), so it has near-zero topical overlap with Seal-0's Entertainment/Sports/Science/Aviation trivia questions. 110/111 questions retrieved 0 search docs in both modes; the composer's OWN judgment (not corpus emptiness) produced the 111th abstention on the 1 question with docs ('Mercury(I) chloride valency' pulled 10 irrelevant 'Mercury'-homonym travel-blog passages -- planet/singer/element mercury, never chemistry -- and correctly declined). No question in this run had search results that were topically on-target but conflicting, so the abstention machinery's CONFLICT-resolution behavior (the actual Seal-0 thesis) was never exercised -- only its NO-COVERAGE behavior was. Confident-wrong rate 0% is real and reproducible, but should not be read as 'SeaWeb resolves conflicting evidence safely' -- it has not yet been tested on a single Seal-0 question where it retrieved evidence AND that evidence conflicted.

bugs_found.symptom: KeyError: slice(None, 10, None) on every prod call
bugs_found.root_cause: SeaWeb gateway/server.py's search_web MCP tool changed its return shape on 2026-07-28 from a bare JSON list to an envelope {"coverage", "results", "note"} (server.py ~line 2095, comment: 'envelope (breaking change, 2026-07-28)'). SeaWebClient.search() still does `for row in rows[:MAX_DOCS]` assuming rows is a list; against the new envelope rows is a dict, and dict[:10] raises KeyError.
